newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian L&H signs deal with Hitachi.
newsitem.headline: Belgian L&H signs deal with Hitachi.

text.p: Belgian Nasdaq-listed technology firm Lernout & Hauspie (L&H) said on Friday that Japan's Hitachi had agreed to use its speech products technology.

It said text-to-speech and automatic speech recognition technology would be used for Hitachi's 32-bit SH-3 processor, the world's top-selling RISC (reduced instruction set computing) microprocessor. L&H gave no financial details.

"Hitachi chose L&H because it produces high-quality speech in many different languages at a very low cost," Matthew Trowbridge, general manager of the European marketing group at Hitachi Europe Ltd, said in the L&H statement.

L&H's text-to-speech technology converts written text into natural sounding speech and will be used in applications that allow travellers to call their PCs and have electronic mail read to them over any telephone.

Its automatic speech recognition will be integrated into processors used in consumer electronics devices, many of which have limited keyboards. It can be used to locate appointments and contacts, enter alphanumeric characters and allow customers to verbally command and control their applications.
